question: Recurrence in miniature: a deterministic world has 1,000 possible states and changes once a second. At most how many seconds before it repeats?
answer: Once a state recurs, determinism repeats all that follows: at most 1,000 seconds.
move: Finite options and endless time make repetition a certainty, not a coincidence.
trap: Assuming it could wander forever without coming back.
hint: Count how many readings you can take before a new state runs out.
steps: Only 1,000 distinct states exist, so two readings must match.
Once a state recurs, determinism repeats all that follows: at most 1,000 seconds.
source: Nietzsche, The Will to Power, section 1066
reference: Nietzsche, The Will to Power, trans. Kaufmann & Hollingdale, Random House, 1967, section 1066
